quote: Humans detect social cheating with much greater reliability than isomorphic violations of abstract logical rules.
content: Relevance theory and cheater detection are rival explanations of a facilitation that neither side disputes, and the essay uses only the facilitation. On the larger charge: the essay's claim is that there is a fact of the matter about which inferences are truth-preserving and which are not, and that no plea changes it — which does not require any of the contested norms named. Conditionalization, regularity and common priors are disputed at the margins; that P(A&B) cannot exceed P(A) is not, and neither is the claim that wanting something does not make it likely, which is the law the essay is invoking.

quote: For example, one finds religious people defending their beliefs by saying, “Well, you can’t justify your belief in science!”
content: The essay's answer is not foundational and does not need to be. The rationalist's engine and the theist's are both defended circularly at the base; what distinguishes them is that one has a track record of predictions that came out, and a method for finding out when it is wrong, and the other does not — which is the pragmatic reply the annotation says is the honest one and which this book gives at length. Whether the theist can also claim a track record is exactly the question, and it is an object-level question rather than a stalemate about foundations.
